correctness.rationale: The symmetric Gram matrix reduces exactly to the two real equations E S=0, E S²=n. Solving those gives st=n and unique positive shell masses; parity constraints give existence. A finite divisor minimum is exact for every odd n. n=51 is the first strict transition by exhaustive exact enumeration for n=3..49 and four divisors at n51. Infinite improvement follows from a positive-coefficient rational recurrence and an inductive inequality; verifier independently checks exact finite matrices and the symbolic coefficient identity. No finite experiment substitutes for the analytic proof.

General relative-design language is a serious residual bibliographic risk but no decisive prior implication was identified.

value.rationale: Exact tight finite Walsh sampling is a natural stable-reconstruction invariant. A single full shell necessarily loses one band direction, so determining the precise arithmetic ability of two complete shells to restore all directions is a structural classification. The divisor minimum also quantifies the smallest symmetric measurement support, and the n51 first transition plus its infinite n≡3 mod6 continuation is a meaningful change in which geometry is more economical, rather than an arbitrary computed slice.
